Termination rule: counts only where it took a reservation this order created. The Tribe's newspaper Smoke Signals (November 1, 1989, p. 1) says 597 acres of reservation land remained at termination in 1954 and that tribal land other than the cemetery and a few plots was sold. So the Act ended trust over what remained of the reservation this 1857 order made: the breach qualifies and status broken stands.
Grand Ronde Treaties page: reservation established by executive order June 30, 1857, originally 61,000 acres, reduced by federal actions in the late 1800s.
Grand Ronde Termination & Restoration page: quote exact; Restoration Act November 22, 1983 (P.L. 98-165); 9,811 acres regained September 9, 1988.
Grand Ronde Reservation Act, P.L. 100-425, 102 Stat. 1594 (govinfo): approximately 9,811.32 acres held in trust and made the reservation.
